title: Understanding N-gram Encoding
text: N-gram encoding involves breaking down sequences into smaller overlapping segments. Consider how this might affect the representation of DNA sequences.

title: Consider the Nature of DNA Sequences
text: DNA sequences are linear and do not wrap around. Think about how N-gram encoding might misinterpret this structure.

title: Analyzing Overlapping Segments
text: When using N-gram encoding, overlapping segments are created. For example, the sequence ATGCA would be broken into ATG, TGC, and GCA. Why might this be problematic?

title: Non-Consecutive Segments
text: N-gram encoding might capture non-consecutive segments as words. For instance, ATGCA could suggest AGA. Why is this a concern?

title: Wrap-Around Segments
text: Consider how N-gram encoding might incorrectly capture wrap-around segments, such as TGG from GGTT. Why is this an issue?
